title: Face blindness (prosopagnosia): what it is and how people cope

sources.title: Face blindness may be more common than previously thought
Prosopagnosia: face blindness and its association with neurological disorders

facts.text: Face blindness, or prosopagnosia, is a condition in which people have great difficulty recognizing faces.
Developmental face blindness is present from birth without brain damage and can run in families.
Acquired face blindness results from damage to the brain, for example after a stroke or injury.
People with face blindness often rely on other cues, such as voice, the way a person walks, or hairstyle; a change such as a new haircut can defeat these cues.
They rely heavily on context, so they may fail to recognize a familiar person met in an unexpected place.
Failing to recognize people can be embarrassing and may be mistaken by others for rudeness or coldness.
Many people with the developmental form do not realize they have it until adulthood and may blame a poor memory instead.
There is no cure, although training can make face recognition somewhat easier.
